There are mechanics but they don't overtake gameplay like modern games. The execution isn't bad either. Combos are fairly simple in execution and not overwhelmingly challenging. The neutral is such a fun experience.  You start out playing at a snail-like pace because the weight of your decisions means life or death in this game. There are some BIG damaging buttons in this game. Once you have an understanding of things the game becomes faster while you balance on the tightrope of death.  Because of that, this game teaches players the importance of fundamentals in fighting games. You cannot rely on gimmicks or neutral skips to win rounds. There are comeback mechanics but it's a one time only so you cannot use them as a crutch.
I love this game and I wish to have it locally played but the game is unfortunately a Discord fighter. The majority of the player base is on Xbox as well. The reason for that is there is a 120fps version of the game. That version is only on Xbox (there had to be some licensing deal for exclusivity). So there is a great community out there constantly having brackets, lobbying, and even tournaments at majors but it's not the easiest to get into. The reason why I said more support from SNK is because they took a while to upgrade the net code for this game. COVID showed fighting game developers how important net code is to keeping their games alive (besides Tekken Michael Murray and Harada are in denial). So I feel like SNK shifted focus on their newer fighters rather than save the project. I hope to see another installment for the series because Samsho's historically a big franchise for fighting games. I would buy the game and grab a few friends to buy it when it goes on sale (it's on sale a lot). The community are some great people around the world so don't be afraid to ask for help. [b]nofrills solitaire[/b] (formerly [b]nofrills klondike solitaire[/b], still called that in the library) is just that: a simple card game for an affordable price, now with [b]spider[/b], [b]freecell[/b] and [b]scorpion[/b] variants, on top of the original [b]klondike[/b].

the presentation is actually a lot better than one would expect and it took a while for some of the basics to make it in, but it's pretty good now. except for the text-free ui, though even that got improved over time. there's a pdf manual linked on the store page to explain what's what, but [b]if your game needs a 10-page document, text-free nonsense clearly doesn't work anymore.[/b]

while the graphics look too flashy at first, especially for something that claims not to have any bells and whistles in its title, it's a really pleasant sight to behold. the music is great too, but unfortunately [b]you have to skip tracks manually[/b] when you've had enough of a song. it's intentional and I have no idea why. the [b]loops are also very short[/b], so as good as the tracks are, they get repetitive really fast. more can be unlocked by completing certain achievements, while others unlock more cardbacks.

windowed mode and volume settings got patched in, and now klondike has [b]1 and 3 card modes[/b] and [b]shuffle[/b], and when everything's uncovered, even [b]auto-complete[/b], skipping some busywork. without shuffle it took me about 2 hours to finally win, but that's in the past. oh, and your wins are also shown now in the main menu. [b]spider[/b] has 1-, 2- and 4-suit variants, can be changed in the menu and by what else than clicking the random pyramid at the bottom while playing...

[b]controls improved a lot with the addition of drag & drop mode.[/b] before that single click was the name of the game, one to select a card, another to put it where you want it to go, no such thing as a double click. I guess it's down to personal preference whether you like this or the dragging method more, but the way clicking works here is a bit problematic because when a card is clicked that can go to one of the foundations, it won't wait for you to choose a destination but automatically go there. so if you wanted to move it somewhere else, you have to click on it again on the top, then move it elsewhere.

shortly after release the game was already recommendable with a few caveats, but all fixed up and even expanded, [b]it's a definite two thumbs up[/b]. looks good, plays well and doesn't cost much, even though the price doubled after the additional game modes got patched in for free for existing owners. [b]undo/redo[/b] also got patched in, but if only there were tooltips or an in-game manual...

EDIT:
The dev listens very much to the gamers and everything is included now and every known bug is solved. So I would like to give two thumbs up (: !

STORY: The story, while open to interpretation, is amazing. Without going into too much detail to avoid spoilers, it perfectly captures what the name might already suggest. This isn't necessarily a bad game, and if I could leave a neutral rating I would. I went in expecting a Choose Your Own Adventure game in the vein of those old, wonderful books. I got something a little different. I replayed the beginning ~10 minutes multiple times doing all the different choices I could to see roughly what the game was like.

[h1]Pros[/h1]
+The writing is excellent, and what I briefly saw there were no grammatical or spelling errors. The writing wasn't complicated and I expect most people who can read will be able to play and enjoy all the writing of this game. Despite not being complicated I found it engaging, but..

[h1]Cons[/h1]
-Although the writing is good and engaging, I'm much more of a science fiction fan and this didn't particularly interest me. I'm sure it gets more sci-fi'y later, but I wasn't really drawn in to start, exacerbated by my next issue.

-The vast majority of choices don't seem to matter at all. The game boasts over 2000 choices, but all except like 2 of them don't matter in the beginning, and you'll make 15-20 in this time period. At the beginning you have the choice of visiting 1 of 2 people. Which person you choose seems to determine your next step in the story. Who you choose first slightly changes how the story plays out with the other, but it doesn't seem to matter. This is my greatest issue with the game and why I don't feel motivated to play it. I want ALL my choices to matter, like they did in those old books. Instead almost every choice leads you along the same path if you reload and take the other one. In the CYOA books almost every choice you made sent you on a different, unique adventure. Only rarely would your choices converge in those books, and I loved it. I would have over a dozen bookmarks so whenever I reached a story end I could go back and make a different choice to see what changes. Here nothing of value changes. At the end I'll have a spoiler section detailing various early game choices and how they have no impact. The reason so few choices matter is likely due to my next issue.

-You can't die in this game, and there aren't any bad endings. No matter what choices you make you can continue to the end. This is horrible for a CYOA story, because it means so many paths must converge, thus meaning very few choices actually matter, or you'll have virtually no choices to make or else you'll have an impossible amount of story branches. If you're going to go this route I would rather they remove all choices that don't actually matter, and keep only the ones that will change your story path. Or at least have the choices that matter be a different color so I know which choices to pay attention to and to change on future playhtroughs.

-Bafflingly you have 1 save file. That's right, just one. In a huge story like this where there's supposed to be "10 story arcs" having only a single save is criminal.

-There's a function to rewind to your previous choice, but it doesn't allow you to make a different choice so it's pointless. Your only other option is to restart the whole game. Thankfully there's a button that skips the story ahead to the next choice, but it quickly gets tedious, even in the early game.

-Moti, your AI assistant, is really annoying how she constantly pops up to interrupt the story flow with meaningless comments.

-There is absolutely no backstory about yourself, or either of the two people you are asked to choose between meeting. It seems this information may get slowly dished out as the story continues, but still it's a bad way to start a story. Surely there could be an optional prologue exposition dump from the main menu (if this game had one which it doesn't).

-+The music is simple and boring, but then again that could be good so it doesn't distract from the text. Sound effects are rare but do add to the story, such as a door creaking open or the sound of a gunshot.

[h1]Closing thoughts + spoilers[/h1]
The game is cheap, about the cost of a used paperback. If the premise intrigues you, and my complaints don't scare you, and you like reading, then this game is for you. If you are like me and wanted a CYOA book in game form, you will be severely disappointed.

Early ~10 minute game spoilers![spoiler]At the start you have the choice between meeting Delores or Professor Sole. No matter what it seems Sole is killed. Delores also gets attacked but I'm pretty sure she escapes. I mostly explored going to Sole's first. Arrive at Soles and you can examine his overpacked suitcase which reveals he's planning a trip to a certain place, or you can ignore it. This doesn't matter because later when Sole is killed you search his body without choice and learn of that place anyway. As he's dying you can choose to stem the blood flow or try to listen to what he has to say. No difference. Before this you can ask him a if it's him or another choice I forget, but they don't matter. After this he asks you to come closer and you can comply or not, it makes no difference. But if you do come closer you have the choice to examine his diary or ignore it, but this doesn't matter. After he's killed you get a gun and can choose to carefully approach the house exit in pursuit of the murderer, or charge after them. It doesn't matter. You then can choose between chasing one of two people, and while they do lead to slightly different paths they converge exactly the same. Chase down the alley and you have the choice to shoot the fence lock twice, or attempt climbing it twice. Both have the same outcome of you getting knocked unconscious and the murderer taking your gun (I wonder if it's ever explained why he just doesn't kill you). Reload and go after the guy on the bus where you get more choices that make no difference ending with you getting knocked unconscious and losing the gun. This is where you have the choice of meeting Delores or going back to Sole's to look for research notes. It didn't seem to matter which I did in the grand scheme but I didn't play much beyond those choices. Go meet Delores and you can get to the house and search it before the cops show up. I chose to leave before finding the itinerary so I don't know what would change if it actually lets me find it. If you go back to Sole's you have to go to Delores' anyway but the police are there and won't tell you anything.[/spoiler]

Dr. Milo's Revenge is a low effort troll comedy horror game. The gameplay consists of... finding things, avoiding a slow moving doctor cat thing and running when said doctor cat thing spots you. Revolutionary game mechanics I know. 

You start off as a science person who is doing unknown research in a science facility in the middle of a snowy tundra. The power is off and it is up to you to turn on the generators to bring back power to your science facility. One of your fellow researchers "Dr. Milo" is also mysteriously missing. Dr. Milo being a cat doctor hybrid wielding a pipe? like weapon. Milo will try to stop you at each area where a generator is located. By stopping you, I mean, running at you very slowly while making a very loud earrape level sound, that is honestly the best thing about the game, it's a fucking terrifying sound. When he catches you, Milo smacks you with his pipe. You can take multiple hits from his pipe so it's not difficult to survive him. 

There are some strats I discovered when dealing with Milo. In 2 of the 3 generator areas, you can have him chase you across the snowy tundra for basically as long and far as you need, just keep triggering him. Once you get him a decent distance from your target location, you can run around him and head back. He will slowly walk back to the generator area but it will take a couple minutes, giving you time to basically complete everything. In fact I'm pretty sure each area has it's own Milo, so hypothetical you could have all 3 Milo's meet each other. I'm not sure what happens when you do this (haven't tested the theory yet) but the results could be catastrophic. 

The first generator room to your left is the only challenging one because the door locks behind you. You basically just have to find 2 keys while avoiding Milo. If you can survive this, then the next two areas are a give away because you can just lure Milo half way across the continent and then go back and solve the puzzles. Puzzles which include, finding a key, opening a door, grabbing bolt cutters and using them on a chained up door. The other puzzle is turning wheels on pipes in a certain order. Groundbreaking puzzles I know.

After all the generators are on you will be treated to a final showdown with Milo. You head back to main base to use the telecommunications to contact a helicopter. I walked in and Milo spotted me, I ran to get away but he wouldn't stop chasing me. I ran halfway across the ridiculously large map and back until I ran inside the barn area, ran into the Milo of that area, he hit me, I turned a corner and lost both of the Milos. Made my way back to the main base, contacted the helicopter, went to the pad and beat the game.  I'm honestly not sure how to get past the final Milo without losing him inside the barn or another generator area. He killed me the first time I played and there are NO SAVES so you have to start from the beginning... which is really, really painful and kind of killed me on the inside. 

Once you beat the game, you unlock Nightmare Mode. Which is just an impossible troll version of the normal game. There is no way to beat it. If you glitch out Milo and make your way to the telecommunications room, you're locked in that room and cannot leave. 

I would not recommend Dr. Milo's Revenge. The only enjoyment I got out of it was playing while a friend watched me over Discord as I suffered through the grind of trolling Milo halfway across the map as his awful earrape noise blasted every couple seconds. If you wanna entertain yourself and some friends, buy this game for a $1 during a steam sale. It 100% is not worth $5, a reminder that "Tattletale", "The Music Machine" and the first "Welcome to The Game" are also $5, please buy those games instead, those are good games.

This is a fun arcade racer where speed is the name of the game. Z-Race looks really good. Those who loved the WipEout series should definitely take a closer look at Z-Race, because there is almost no games of this kind left.

This is a really fun, well done VR Racing game. I prefer being in the driver seat and usually avoid 3rd person, this one being the exception.  The ship design is sleek and very "wipeout", as are the tunnel style stages. (the game is not completely tunnels btw sometimes you get a little open space between tunnels) Though I feel that it sort of ends there with the comparison.

 If you have ever seen the Dis movie "Flight of the Navigator" piloting here seems similar. The ship was flown by 2 domed pads that floated on arms to the sides of the pilot. To roll left (slight turn) you "roll" your dominant hand left and vice versa. Your yaw can also be used to turn but will cause you to slow/drag, same for pitch (up/down). Basically you fly as if your hand is the ship. No external controller or flight stick/HOTAS is used for this.

Typically being a first person player I have noted that I tend to keep my dominant hand to the center, of the top of my chest, close to my body (like a chicken wing) and find better reaction and control here. It's also a little like having your head on top of your ship.

Can this be played seated? My opinion is somewhat. A lot of courses will require you to actually turn left, right, up, or down, (diagonally at time) I recommend standing so that you can be best positioned to make these turns. Most of the movements made will be slight to avoid tunnel hazards, the more extreme the turn of your ship the more speed you lose.

I do not get motion sickness from VR but I can see how the speed could cause vertigo for some that haven't toughed their VR legs. Caution advised but not nearly as bad as some games. 

On a side note don't get greedy until you're comfortable the boosts in the rotating floating circles are not worth hitting the hazard behind it.

Highly recommended mainly because the racing is fun, fast, and novel. Hoping to see good things in the future.

Theres a few things i want to note

My first impression from before early access was this was to be something similar to Redout which is one of my favorite VR racing games. I play a lot of racing sims with racing wheels and joysticks, and I am the owner and lead developer at Piece by Piece XR Development where I develop VR-focused cockpit games giving me a strong understanding of cockpits, movement, and ergonomics for VR users. 

The first note from me is to avoid palmar deviation, unfortunately, z-race focuses on a control motion that causes palmar deviation through the primary control method. Lifting your chosen hand up in front of you while rotating your hand 90 degrees inward becomes uncomfortable very quickly. After a couple of restarts, I could not get it to correct to the designed ergonomics of the controller of thumb vertical, so I have to assume this was by design. This made my arm both tired very quickly and became uncomfortable very quickly. After only 20ish minutes I was not able to continue playing as there was a significant amount of discomfort. 

The second note, I understand the purpose of holding the car in your chosen hand and moving it in the direction you want to go was to help reduce motion sickness, I work in VR daily and I do not experience motion sickness in the slightest, however, my significant other is susceptible to motion sickness but not tremendously sensitive to it. I'd place them in the average/new VR user space. My point for this is to express that they were able to play z-race for a maximum of 30 seconds before pulling the headset off and having to cool off for 10 minutes. An issue that was not had with redouts in cockpit view. 

My third note which is purely opinion, I would have strongly preferred the approach of being inside the cockpit, camera attached to the desired ship, or at least having control over the ship via virtual joysticks(similar to no man’s sky), gamepad (similar to redout), or controller thumb-stick support(same as gamepad but mapped to VR controllers). I strongly feel that not approaching one or more of these leaves a significant amount of the audience of racing sim enthusiasts behind. I understand the choice made, however personally and professionally I would suggest one of the other approaches as a potential option. In its current state, of course, being early access I understand limiting what's provided. However, there is no mention of other options for the future of the game. If these were to be added I’d happily buy the game again, however, as it is currently I will be refunding it as I felt tremendous discomfort and I just am not interested in racing in this way.

You have a wide range of aircrafts to pick from, and are able to upgrade the stats of each ship. Giving you tons of possibilities. The ships also have sponsors of some of the top content creators. Have a favorite YouTuber, jump in their ship and win some races. The game also has a wide range of race tracks to go through, each posing new challenges.

This is one of the top VR experience I have had in a long time, and would highly recommend it to anyone.

FIRSTLY: It is possible that the devs have shifted almost entirely to rigging this game for quest support. This could be a good thing.

Anyway, this game is just incredible in overarching concept and design. It feels absolutely amazing to play--stimulating, competitive, beautiful, challenging, enrapturing. In general this game is perfect and I have no complaints.

-only 5 maps with variations
-voice lines get repetitive quickly
-no settings menu, in-game restart/quit option, hyper-minimal UI
-matches in a new map tend to start you finishing 10th in the first match and 1st in the second due to rank calibration, which slightly deflates the initial feeling of challenge and accomplishment
-map designs in terms of added challenge (obstacles) are simplistic and universal, all function with minimal fashion, not too many thematically coherent obstacles that match with the maps (the Quest beta seems to be fixing this problem) 

REGARDLESS: This dev team seriously deserves the resources to make this a much bigger and higher quality game. Itching for a good platforming game that takes an unusual angle of how the gameplay for said platformer plays out, Mighty Fling is a hard tower-based climber that bears the spirit of Jump King's most revered difficulty but tones it down in a couple of unique ways that makes it surprisingly more approachable for those looking to dip their toes into the more challenging platforming games out there.

For starters, you control a white ball that starts off in the bottom of a very tall tower whereby you escape from the cage it's inside using momentum brought forward by a tried-and-tested 'click and drag' approach to aim where the ball goes and how far it goes via the strength of it determined by how far you drag said click from it's original spot, after which the ball will, indeed, be flung instantly in that direction!

Now what makes this a couple of steps easier (or, as some of the more cynical of gamers out there would likely claim, more 'fair) is that a most handy visual indicator of where your shot and the trajectory of it will align roughly, as this can be used to give those in need of that extra assistance a little fighting chance in some of the more difficult platforming obstacles (of which the first proper challenge is not even that far away from the bottom of the tower!) that await within the heights of the tower.

Furthermore, a perk that Jump King does not have is the ability for one to adjust their ball's direction mid-flight, as this allows for quick-second decision-making that could very well save you from a big fall as well as allowing more experienced Mighty Fling players to take shortcuts with the right knowledge and precision, definitely a handy feature to have as far as how challenging this platformer can be!

Speaking of which, the overall challenge from this game is certainly a couple of leagues below that of Jump King's much harder DLC towers, albeit I would make the argument that this tower here has it's difficulty spread across certain parts as some segments of the tower are noticeably more difficult to pass than others, as each fall has the risk of sending your ball a great distance down if your luck is bad enough to be in the wrong spot! Although it is a relief that the halfway point does offer a near-guarantee safe checkpoint of sorts, which should ease the anxieties of those dreading going from near the top of the tower all the way right down to the bottom again!

Now, despite being a pretty good platformer of the vertical kind that has a unique style of gameplay to it that also balances challenge with extra aids in the form of a visual indicator and the ability to fling again mid-flight, Mighty Fling does have a few flaws in that it is surprisingly easy to accidentally quit your current session and restart the whole game from scratch, with no confirmation button in sight. Also the sound and resolution settings reset for me each time I booted up the game here, having to manually change them back every time I got back on to give it another shot.

Finally, it is rather disappointing that there is no 'secret' extra-hard content as the last segment does give a taste of what truly difficult platforming for Mighty Fling can be here, as it would have been a nice incentive for New Game+ players to have to go back up to the top of the tower a second time, only to discover a whole new extension has been added to it alongside more of the witty and charming characters that this game has spread across the scale of the tower itself!

Otherwise though, I would safely recommend this unique platformer that takes some form of inspiration from Jump King for those looking to see if they have what it takes without being too insane of a challenge for the slightly more casual of players!

TLDR Version:

• A unique platformer that offers a new perspective into the scene with controlling a white ball through 'click and drag' methods that is easy to pick up but hard to master (+)
• Challenging gameplay that rewards those with patience and determination whilst being easier than it's inspiration, Jump King, by adding in a visual indicator for more casual gamers (+)
• Lovely retro pixel graphics that help one to reminiscent about the older gaming days whilst being polished up with more modern software and techniques (+)
• The ability to affect the direction of the ball mid-flight allows for quick saves from otherwise bad flings whilst also doubling as a method for professional players to take shortcuts with added risk and reward (+)
• Fun characters that are spread throughout the tower that add charm to the world of Mighty Fling (+)

I just finished the game and I can share my experience:

- settings interface too empty (3 options that don't even save when we exit the game),
- no change of scenery and a very short map,
- no achievements, so there's no point in actually playing the game yet,
- no checkpoints and changes in scenery to make progress visible and the game gets boring quickly :(
- the game's difficulty changes too much (the game's difficulty varies throughout the game, it's hard at the beginning, then it gets easier, and at the very end it's definitely too hard).
- the controls are a bit strange and even broken at times:
(- the mouse off the screen blocks aiming the ball,
- the ball's texture breaks when the ball falls to the ground,
- when we hold the left mouse button while falling, we cannot aim the ball on the ground and when we release the LMB, the ball flies left or right,
- the camera refuses to move up in the most important moments of the game,
- sometimes the ball bounces off the wall and sometimes it doesn't,
- the ability to bounce off the wall when falling is useless and hinders more than it actually helps.)
I hope that the author is still working on the game and will update it in the future because the concept of the game is really good. I'll be waiting :P

In super-slow, long, trial-and-error puzzles that softlock by design.
Complete heresy.

I like to spend my precious time actively solving puzzles, not passively waiting for slow animations, transitions, and resets.

As it stands, I could take no more than a few puzzles before leaving with a resounding yawn.

In summary this game is difficult, very difficult.
Great for any member of the family to play, but younger children will have problems throwing it very far, which is required for some sections.
There are easier ways of getting past some puzzles, if you want to know how then read the spoilers at the end of the review.

It took me 13.2 hours to complete, this is mainly because if you miss some of the targets you will end up back at the beginning or back at approx. halfway through. It is also because I spent a while just looking around at the scenery, which is very well done and nice to explore.
Gameplay is very good, and it is easy to play. The ability to practice with the red stone is essential, especially when doing the accuracy and placing challenges. 
Having a lot of available space to move about is helpful when getting to some targets.
There are areas where the stone will turn back to red if your throwing arm goes out of the map edge. This confused me for a while as you can’t see it change colour, you just end up not moving. You can also look and walk through the walls and see upper and lower levels.
After making it to the goal you get a nice trophy, visible on the games start page.
About that start menu, make sure you click continue and not new game by mistake.
You cannot save more than one game ie. Only one player can play and save their progress. This is a shame if someone else wants to play.

Warning spoilers follow:
You can walk over to targets to make things easier. There is no need to stay in the red throwing zone marked on the floor.
Placing the stone down rather than throwing it is a big part of the game nearer the end. Look at the stone and notice one side of it is flatter than the other. So, it will not roll when put down.
When at the section where you must go down steps, this can be made easier by resetting the floor level in the VR settings to about waist height. Then move it back after.
Having a chair to stand on helps in some areas but be careful not to bang your hand on the ceiling as the guard setting does not have a height warning.

A game involving a genetically enhanced cyborg penguin who uses ocean-related power-ups to help fight waves of invading aliens is a suitably bonkers theme for this retro-inspired shoot em up that proves to be a lot of fun.

Sound is particularly good with some suitably creepy demonic effects and great music (including a choice of soundtracks). The action is decent-paced and fun, It offers a reasonable challenge for the average gamer and (most crucially of all) is good enjoyable to play. It's really captured that critical "just one more go" addictiveness. I genuinely kept thinking "i'll just have one more go, then I'll write that review"... and kept saying that until over an hour of "just one more go's" had passed!

Gameplay mostly feels well-balanced and fair - if you die, it's (usually) your fault. It's well-paced, with nicely developed levels that gradually get trickier. It's not the hardest of games - a single afternoon's play saw me (hardly the most accomplished of gamers) beat it, but beating it twice unlocks Boss Rush and Survival mode and these (plus the challenge of beating your high score) will certainly keep me coming back to it when I fancy a quick blast.

The biggest issue with Super Psy Penguin lies with the graphics. Whilst they are imaginative and reasonably varied, the colouring is quite dull. They don't really stand out against the backgrounds (particularly some of the moving backgrounds like Level 1's clouds) and this can make them very hard to see - something that can prove fatal in a game like this. 

Bottom line: Super Psy Penguin is a decent and fun retro-themed shooter. It's not going to trouble the acknowledged champs of the genre, but it's a long, long way from being the worst example of its kind and offers plenty of scope for enjoyment. It's probably going to struggle to attract attention in a crowded indie market, but at £3.99, it offers fair value for money, and a decent blast. If you do pick it up, you won't regret it. I certainly don't.

Playing through Simply Puzzles: Junctions was fun for me. It is a minimalistic numbers puzzle game and as such is very reminiscent of Tametsi and the Hexcells series even though its puzzles are not as unique and rather generic. Yet there has not been another similar game in quite a while that was able to keep my attention all the way through to the end.

Junctions puzzles consist of a board with a rectangular grid and some numbers on the grid junctions which tell you how many lines have to touch that number. Each square of the grid has to be filled with a diagonal line so obviously there are only two options to fill any given square. On top of that simple rule the player is not allowed to form any given shape with the lines on the board, i.e. there must not be a closed "loop" of lines. Finally and most importantly, none of the puzzles require any guessing!

What intriguied me about the game was exploriong all the different facets of "starting clues". Aside form the obvious clues, e.g. a 0 or a 4 on the board, there are plenty of other deductions that can be made in order to start filling an untouched section of the board and finding those was very satisfying. Yet the amount of deductions to apply is limited and with 100 puzzles to complete some may find the gameplay a bit repetitive. As mentioned before, Junctions does not reach the craftsmanship of such games as Tametsi or Hexcells.

There would be some room for improvement. Most important for me would be a feature that lets you highlight a specific continuous line on the board, especially in the later puzzles of the game. It can be quite challenging to figure those out on your own on a board with about 100 squares that are mostly filled. I know such feature from conceptis puzzles games and it would simply facilitate solving the puzzles as opposed to progressing the puzzle solution.

Nonetheless, I find Junctions much better than plenty of other minimalistic number puzzle games out there and as such it deserves my recommendation. It took me a little over 5 hours to complete all puzzles. For a price of 2.39€ that's a good amount of content.

Bought it after seeing the trailer posted on Reddit. The concept seems interesting and the gameplay shown in the trailer looks fun, but as of 2020-10-26, this game does *not* deliver.

First off, the menu is clunky and doesn't have information like key bindings, the "back" button is non-function on the settings menu. There is no "quit" option, you need to alt-f4 out.

Going into a game, the opening cinematic has your character shooting zombies, but they couldn't be bothered to actually have him point his gun at them, he just magically shoots them while in his "idle" animation. You get plunked into wave 1 without any explanation, which isn't terrible, I can figure out how to shoot zombies.

In the break after wave 1, a timer pops up, which is the only indication the wave is over. No idea how to build anything, or research anything, the NPC just sits in a chair, no idea if I can interact with him in any way. I start mashing all the keys to see if anything happens and mistakenly start the next wave by pressing "N".

In further waves, other NPCs show up and you can eventually buy other weapons and build things. Your money is basically unreadable in the bottom left corner. Once you place barriers or whatnot there is no way to get rid of them, so you'd better get it right the first time.

The gunplay is very unsatisfying. Reload times feel extremely long and the gun just disappears off screen during the reload. All the guns I tried seemed to sound the same and do more or less the same damage. If I buy a high-calibre hunting rifle, I'd expect it to produce a satisfyingly loud "boom" rather than the same noise as a pistol. Aiming down the sights seems to do little to nothing as far as accuracy. The sound effects and "voice acting" are, charitably, placeholders (I hope).

Movement is clunky, invisible walls seem to block you from jumping certain places. Your run speed feels like a leisurely stroll, rather than actually running.

Anyway, wrapping up, this game does not seem finished at all. It *could* be really fun, but needs a lot of work to get there. I'm refunding my purchase and hope that sometime in the future they get it to what I hoped it would be.

I'm never quite sure what to think of detective games. I'm always looking to have the "eureka!" moments that are depicted on film and TV, but they never seem to come for me. More often than not, I'm just bumbling around, hoping to hit on whatever line of questioning the developer intended me to take.

Lockheart Indigo is very clever about mitigating some of these irritations. First off, the game has a built-in hint system (the Oracle's Chamber), which can give you direction if you're lost. Also, as another reviewer mentioned, the game's central characters and various lock types are all color-coded - if something isn't colored, there's a good chance you don't need to interact with it. However, there is some good information that can be gleaned by interacting with grayscale objects/individuals as well. Additionally, there is a book on the first floor that tells you exactly which areas are on each floor. I wrote this down, and referenced it as I moved through the game. The game includes multiple telephones on various floors that can be used as save points, and Beatris can teleport from one to another to get around more quickly.

I got through most of interrogations easily enough, but I never knew exactly which "fact" to present to a suspect to begin the persuasion minigame. I couldn't ascertain the logic here. The game is kind enough to provide a simple "read" button during the interrogation so Beatris can reveal what she's been able to glean about the psychological characteristics of the suspect. As a result, once the persuasion mini-game begins in earnest, you'll have a good idea of how to proceed. It did take me a few tries to complete the final interrogation, and I felt that the checkpoint was a little "off" here. I got tired of walking up the stairs, heading down the path through the multiple arches, and watching the "cut scene" play out before I could begin the interrogation anew. 

I appreciated the game's Game Boy aesthetic, and found the mansion itself to be well-designed. Although it may initially be overwhelming, by the end of the game's brief runtime you'll have a good idea of how to reach any of its 100 rooms. I have to give developer Harmless praise for the game's logo, combining Beatris' distinctive hair with the many keys she must acquire to explore the home. It's exquisite.

I think it could benefit the developer to provide a few more clues as to what is happening in the game's final explanatory scene (where the player is not playing as Beatris). I'm pleased with the conclusions I drew, but it took me quite a bit of rumination to arrive there. Perhaps things could be made a bit more explicit?

Lastly - and maybe I missed something here -[spoiler]does Beatris turn off the radio (that she has been wearing to converse with Aya) before or during her chat with Yvon? Did she forget that she had it on?[/spoiler]As this decision is spoken about a lot in the game, I think that perhaps the characters should address the concern I had above. Although I liked the ongoing conversation between Beatris and Aya, I felt that perhaps it'd be better if this were strictly audio. I know that the game as it currently is has no voice-acting, but it could be distracting to pay attention to where you are going (especially while trying to push crates around) and also pay attention to this dialogue.

I can cautiously recommend Lockheart Indigo. Although it's not the best detective game I've played (Subsurface Circular or Sherlock Holmes: Crimes & Punishments likely takes that crown), it's got an interesting tale to tell, and you can "hear" it for only five dollars.

I had a lovely time with the game for its two hour running time. It's basically a detective game where you gather clues and then use them to interrogate suspects a la L.A. Noire or Ace Attorney Investigations if you've ever played them. 

Unfortunately, it leans more on the L.A. Noire side of things in that you never really have to think too hard about what you're doing or try to reconstruct the crime in your head as there is information that is always hidden from you and there's no mechanics geared toward logically trying to piece together what happened like Investigations does with its logic mechanic. Plus, the penalty for not picking the right options is just being sent back a short ways or having to start the conversation over from the beginning which gives the player the incentive to randomly guess options rather than thinking about them.

I don't want to seem like I'm being too harsh because I did enjoy this game, I recommend it, and I'd say it's worth the full asking price. The artwork and animation is fantastic for the interrogation scenes and the story is enjoyable if really short. Plus, I do really like Beatris as our protagonist. I like how she's trying to be a seasoned Poirot-type even though she's still pretty young and in over her head. I also like how crass she is when she thinks to herself and cuts loose.

What I'm really trying to say is that I'd like to see a longer sequel someday that expands on the mechanics this game lays out. And I'd like to see more of Beatris and her adventure in this odd, sci-fi version of the 60s. Maybe even progress into the 70s and 80s if they so desire.

Franchise Hockey Manager Hockey is this the game we can come to love?  Does the 2D engine features compare to EHM?

The pure and straight answer is no.  I really feel like OOTP really dropped a big opportunity to win some support on this product.  For me here are many turnoffs on this game as I will go into detail.  

The nice graphical map is fine for scouting prospects.  Where it faults is how do you scout the short list.  In prior version you were able to assign both players and  scouts to the short for reporting.  The option to assign a scout to the short list does not seam to be available in this latest version.  So now instead of using the short list now you have a watch list.  If the short list is not applicable anymore why keep it as an option.  

The menu system is still the same as the prior version I don't love it or hate it.   Does take some time  getting use to.

Database issues.... Yes they still exist.  I started a game in the QMJHL and right out of the gate I notice issues with the roster.  My roster showed players on my active and depth list but for some reason they were assign to another team within the league.  The first assumption was the player was on a loan to another team.  This was not the case, as the only option I had was to trade for the player.  I checked the the players rights status and notice my team was the owner.  So how can another team own this player when I own his rights?  According to OOTP "It looks like there's a database issue with a few players who have moved between QMJHL teams this season".  These types of issues should not occur in a 7th generation product.  It gets better.  One of my players obtains a major injury fractured hip which causes him to be on the IR for several months.  Remember this is a major injury.  Two months later the development report comes out and this player receives increase in acceleration.  What?  I could understand the month the player was injured to receive some kind of bonus but how does a player increase in acceleration with said injury, no practice or gameplay an entire month?  OOTP "Injuries significantly reduce development speed, but don't eliminate development entirely - if he was close to improving before the injury, the limited increase that happens while he was hurt can still be enough for him to get another point.". Lets talk about last seconds scoring in the game, geez this will irritate you to no end but it's even better when the opposing team starts getting momentum and you can see what the program logic is doing and know your going to lose.  In addition the goaltender on point shots from defenders don't even move at times (or should I say alot).  This is frustrating beyond belief.  After the faceoff is won by the opposing team defender moves to the middle of the ice and scores shooting the opposite post. This is the first version of the 2D engine and did not expect perfection by any means but this appears to had no play test time.  There are many other issues that I could speak of but wanted to provide a few examples for the sake of time.

Many of these issues have been reported to OOTP for addressing.  At this point I feel more like a play tester than a customer enjoying a product.  I really question their quality control methods on this or other products they produce.  This product does have promise but they need to get the basic programming logic resolved to make this a suitable product.  This is a complete utter failure on execution.  After playing this product I will not purchase a future FHM game until all major issues have been resolved.

Expect a jump similar to going from 4X strategy games to Grand strategy games. Having come from the console games myself, I must say I'm particularly happy with my leap of faith, but do keep an open mind.

- As pointed out by the developers, in its current state, the 2D simulation will lead to slightly different results than the classic simulation. Most notably, expect lower shot totals. I asked for a refund since $45 is a lot of money for me, but I will definitely be back when you guys smooth out the bugs! :)
It's getting much closer to being a true replacement for the old EHM games. It get's better with each iteration.

Franchise Hockey Manger 7 is a very good game. It takes a while to get into it, but once it ''clicks'' you will love it. Anybody that loves GM Modes or franchise modes and loves hockey will love this game. Please give this game a few hours before you abandon, I promise that after 2-3 hours, you will love it. 

The updates of FM7 from FM6 are good. I don't use 2D mode and I've never used it (either in FM7 or EHM), but the other improvements are worth it. I don't use any of the coaching features as I like to be the GM and only the GM. I hope they keep releasing the FM games.

I have played a lot of "Team Management" based games over the years as I genuinely prefer that take on sports games. For me I give it a 3.5 - 4 stars out of 5...  I feel it is probably the best of the Ice Hockey Management Sims out there, but it still needs work as some things just don't feel right to me.

- Introduction of 2D Match Engine: 

First off, Step in the right direction and I salute your for your attempt, but after that I found it that bad I actually refuse to use it. First off making the area of the ice larger than what you can see on the screen does not work for me as watching the screen try to move around and keep up with the puck felt very choppy and wasn't very smooth. I also felt this with the movement in the way the puck and players moved, it just felt very false and choppy. The player positioning can also be a bit off with grouping of players, generally just not holding regular positions. The puck covering players numbers added to the fact other than the shirt number you had no way of knowing who was who.

What it needed was a scaled version of the Ice in the middle of the screen (Maybe even from top to bottom down the middle) then on either side of this a list of dressed players / numbers / stats. I get you can see these details on separate screen but to have access to this whilst watching the game play out would be brilliant. I actually think scaling the ice down to fit what you see would remove so much of the choppiness and smooth the engine out (even if you had to keep the stats and players dressed on the separate screen).

- The UI:

Now whilst I don't have any big issues with the UI, at best it is "okay". It does a job, but it also looks a bit bland. I do feel like this could be made more appealing and whilst I don't find it a deal breaker it certainly doesn't help sell it for me.

The above is really, at least right now, my only main points of concern. The game definitely has a lot of potential and for me in terms of Ice Hockey Sims - its the best on the market. I just hope the devs will continue to push on and drive the game forward :)

Crashes multi-year simulations, typically after 8 years.

Trades are limited to 5 assets per side, no 3 ways available.

Very poor detail depth. 

Wish Steam would refund me since it crashes so much...

Game is good but would hold off until they fix whatever issue causes the game to crash to desktop. It is unfortunately unplayable for me at present.

Edit: They fixed the issue, devs are very responsive on reddit and clearly very much care about the community. It is a good hockey sim, lacking some depth and quite rough around the edges but definitely reccomend in its current state,

So where do i begin? Well in short i would not recommend this game in its current state. I might change my mind when they fix stability and bugs.

I been playing FHM since the 5th version and this one is by far the most unstable with frequent crashes that stops you from progressing to game breaking bugs.

The game itself is very dated looking where a Eastside Hockey Manager which is like 6 years old now is better looking and is much more polished! I appreciate that this is small budget and team developers and i can forgive the dated look and engine if it actually worked which in current state it doesn't.

I will carry on playing and buying the newest version when they release them as there's nothing else on the market that is the same ;(

Edit: after playing over 300 hours i still would not recommend the game, game still feels like a beta version! They have fixed the crashes and stability but there is still too many issues with gameplay to enjoy the game as is.

I like this more than the Eastside Hockey Manager as the game came out this year with the up to date rosters and it has a better feel than EHM. I really like the idea of doing a historical start to the game in any season starting from 1917 which is something I never came across in any manager game (I mostly play Football Manager games). The one thing I feel it could be improved would be communication with players and especially coaches (when playing just as a GM) to discuss the vision on how the team should be built. For example head coach asking GM for a better centre or RW etc.

Love this game franchise but this version (7) is absolute trash.
Historical starts dont work as after the first year the stanley cup glitches, your drafts are always linked from screens to be 1 year ahead or behind depending on the way you access it, most players are saved as different ones when looking through team historical stats and of course the biggest flaw of them all, when playing historical mode, around the same season the spanish flu hits, it bugs the game and you can never NEVER trade a player again.

its a great game but it looks like they released a half worked pile of trash this year, i can't believe i spent money on an unplayable game after all the years of great games they have released

So I bought FHM7 for the first time since FHM2.  I asked for a refund.  Here's why:

1.  It does not appear that you can adjust the resolution of the game.  You're stuck with the text size and window size.  And customization appears to be almost non-existant within the NHL game.

2.  Coaching roles are all over the place.  I started in the 2020 season with the New Jersey Devils.  I had 7 assistant coaches, and Mark Recchi was assigned as my Goalie coach?  Huh?

3.  Tooltips - Tooltips linger on the screen, even when you click to a different screen.  Also there is no way to set the delay for tooltips to appear.

4.  The "Lineups" screen can be confusing.  It includes every player in the system.   Not sure why.

5.  OOTPB contains a "Legacy" mode, allowing someone to hire a Head Coach, function as the GM, and still "function" as a head coach even though you have one.  This is not an option in FHM, and if you're someone who tries to play accurate hockey, you know that the role of GM/Head Coach is not an option, so it takes away from emersion a bit.

6.  The 2D engine in game is meh, at best.  The puck will frequently just stop dead on the ice, kind of like playing street hockey with a puck.  Its no where near fluid enough.  And while playing games I felt like far too many shots were from outside of the circles.  There didnt feel like there was any creation at all.

7.  Pressing "CONTINUE" does not sim to the next day.  In fact, there does not appear to be a "sim to next day" option.  The game just goes and goes and goes until you tell it to stop.

This is the same company that makes what I used to regard as the greatest sports management sim of all time: Out of the Park Baseball.  Every year, when someone points out how light years ahead that game is over this one, the response typically is "look at how many more versions there are of OOTPB."  

Well, as someone who has owned every version of OOTPB since OOTP 4, I can tell you that this game does not even compare to OOTP 7 which would have been released in what, 2005?  And yet they still ask $40 for this game.  The gloves are off.  I havent played this since FHM2, for a variety of reasons, and the game is still lacking.  Its been 7 years.  Having something at least somewhat akin to their baseball "brother" would be nice. 

My advice?  If you want to take a shot at it, wait until its on sale.  Its a $20 game, at best, which it has been every single year.  

I'm sure I'll catch flack here for my low playing time, but I tried the game, didnt like it, so I'm moving on.  Might as well do it now so that I don't have to fight for a refund later.

I'm grabbing that refund, spending it elsewhere, and going back to EHM.  I'll try again in another couple of years.

Love that they are essentially mimicking EHM with authentic teams, etc. but the game has a long way to go. After spending a full two weeks playing on average 2 hours a day, one corrupt save wiped out over half the league players. They simply don't exist. Can't begin to describe how frustrating that is. The game has a lot of positives, but bugs are its biggest issue.

UPDATE: Don't bother with this game. I again came back for another stab at FHM 7, but there are so many illogical decisions made by the AI you simply cannot enjoy the game. One, don't bother attempting to play GM-only mode; your HC, even Joel Quennville will endlessly shuffly lines and play players out of position for no good reason. Sign a 3rd line defensive checking center? Expect to see him routinely on the top line at RW playing 23 mins/game. Two, the injury rate is insane. Across 3 seasons  I lost at least one top line F or D to season ending injuries, in addition to constant month-long injuries to key players. Every time you plug a hole, another player goes down. Third, you cannot always fire your coach? The owner will pester you monthly about the teams poor record, but then prevent you from firing your coach who's 2 years into a 3 year contract?? Four, there are serious obvious missed implementations: there is zero notification when UFA signing opens; I totally missed on the biggest UFA options because the game simply simmed right past day 1 of FA. There also seems to be no awareness of the overall draft pick number, just the round its in; teams also don't seem to be aware of their standings when trading picks; generally, the trade system is a simple EA Madden type system: 5 3rd line players somehow can add up to a 1st line player. Lastly (though I could go on), the scout system offers very little engagement, which is often my most favorite part of team management type games. Oh, and also seeing young (23-25 year old) borderline 2nd liners on waivers routinely simply isn't realistic. Nor is it realistic to see a team sign a player and waive him the same day. (Sorry, I went on I think...)

Overall, the game has promise if the developers bring in some real hockey folks who understand/enjoy the team building/management aspects. But, as of now, the game is simply to lacking in overall user experience and logic to be enjoyable given the hours it demands.

FHM7 is the best Hockey Manager game out there imo.  I've logged several hundred hours thru fhm2 until now.. The game is developed by a very small group, meaning it may take several more versions to really make an impact on everyone looking for something in particular they're hoping for that isn't already in the game. If your looking for a smart AI, meaning understanding signings, off-season transactions, trades, drafting that occur... and your like me ... you'll be using the commissioner mode to set things right or reverse trades as it happens thru your simulation career. So be prepared to play the game with your own house rules to really give yourself a challenge. 

The all-new 2D game visual game by game is great but highly unreliable as you watch your players make bizarre plays, shake your head at players clearly out of position etc...  I believe the developers will strengthen this area thru patches and we're hopefully not waiting on the mercy of yearly versions to take advantage of improvements in this area of the game.  Also, If your looking for high customisation, the game is very limited on this area, so it definitely isn't anywhere near it's big brother OOTP Baseball series. 

For example, I'm a fan of the enforcers and scraps that happen in the game,  I'd like to be able to ramp up this setting in particular in all modes, from historical, custom and current but the game is hard-coded to diminish as you progress thru the years if you start in the rough 90's.  

There's a lot the game needs to improve on still but it certainly isn't unplayable.  I highly recommend this game to any and all hockey fans but keep expectations to a minimum and don't get too frustrated if your looking for the amount of depth OOTP Baseball has.  I think in due time, this series will get there but its still got a long ways to go.

Solid 7/10... if this series ever gets to the OOTP level, it will become something legendary !

Love this series and this iteration builds on the previous titles. Some things are still the same, a bit clunky UI but once you spend 100 or so hours it becomes second nature. 

Love the new scouting system, looking forward to further fleshing out as the years go on!

I like this game, but there are many flaws. The instant shop player allowing 3 per day allows you to claim players and trade them for picks sometimes even 1sts. the second major flaw is you can make a trade offer and then later when its approved you can ask the other team to retain 50% of salary and they will always accept even if they can't afford it and without penalty. I have also learned how to game the contract negotiations, which i won't expose here. the salary cap and LTIR is not calculated correctly. salaries of ltir players are still accounted for in the salary cap in real life, but in the game the salary is removed which is incorrect.

Overall, it's pretty good. I spend a lot of hours on it in passive gameplay but it has me constantly thinking about mixing and matching lines to maximize probabilities. I cross my fingers for a create-a-player mode but overall, it's a lot of fun.

This is a fun game. I started getting into hockey a few years ago and my interest and knowledge continue to grow. I primarily use FHM 7 to increase this knowledge and it really enhances my enjoyment watching NHL games lives on TV. Typically, as players do 'things' in the game, I can research them in FHM 7 and learn about their personalities/tendencies and strengths/weaknesses and then see how it plays out in real games. Fun and I feel I am learning quite a bit. I have been a huge fan of the Baseball version of this game for almost a decade now and no doubt this will continue to get better and better every year. I tend to purchase these types of games to support the company so they can continue to make improvements and the community alive and well.

I've been a long time hockey fan and played EA Sports NHL series many years. I've not been playing my playstation for a while and missed the hockey game until I found Franchise Hockey Manager 7. This is exactly what I was looking for and that I played on my playstation in GM Mode except more stats and an overall good experience. This is not really a game more of a simulator if you ever wanted to be a hockey head coach or GM in any league. If you expect to play each game like in EA NHL series you may be disappointed. But for hard core hockey buffs who enjoy the history, the stats and the what ifs this is the game for you.

If you like being an armchair GM in fantasy sports, have a vetted interest in managing all aspects of a team sport and to top it off are a fan of hockey? This game is for you. 

Despite some minor bugs and glitches, which are continuously improved by the devs who are devoted and dedicated, this game shines in delivering the most authentic close to real time life of a GM of a hockey team.

Go ahead forge your own destiny with the new franchise Seattle Kraken, cause yes, they are in this game as well!! 

This game is worth every dollar spent, as the hours will pass and accrue, and you will find satisfaction in building a dynasty of all dynasties!

Being a long time Eastside Hockey Manager player (several thousands hours poured on the 2007 version, more than 500h on the current one), it was at first difficult to adapt to this game, as it is my first experience with the FHM franchise.

I found the UI confusing at first and sometimes not very logical (The shortcuts bar with the tiny logos on the right of the screen comes to mind, I still have problems to use it, IMO it should be on the left and the logos should be bigger). It got a bit better with time though, but I definitly needed several hours to get the hang of it.

There is A LOT of depth to tactics, stats and player history, I just can't fathom the amount of work this must have needed. The immersion is great and I really feel like being part of the hockey world while managing my team. The international side of the game could use an enhancement though, managing a national team in the lower tournaments is not very rewarding at the moment. 

The AI concerning trades and transfers is also very good, I didn't see illogical moves whatsoever, so that's a great point for this type of game.

The 2D engine was very disapointing and subpar compared to EHM, so I currently don't use it and play the text based version (which is great by the way). Kudos to the devs for emplementing it though, while it still needs a lot of work to be able to compete with the EHM one, I read that's it's the first iteration of it for the franchise, and the devs seem to be really working hard on their game, so I have no doubt this will get better over time.

So far my experience is very stable and the most bugs I read about concerned the historical play, which I didn't try yet. The game runs very well and although I read people saying it was really slow I found it quite smooth to be honest.

Overall besides a confusing UI at first and a wonky 2D engine, this game surpasses EHM on many, many key points. EHM being one of my all time favorite game I guess it says a lot.

I definitly recommend FHM to any hockey fan, the game is incredibly deep, the devs are working hard and regularly update their product, and I really enjoy my experience so far. It is indeed the best hockey management game on the market.

I can't wait to see what the future holds for this franchise, it's very promising and I'll definitly support what comes next.
If you are upset about nhl 21, consider this game as an alternative. Not only is it more in depth  but it also has very little bugs and flaws. Highly reccomened

Franchise Hockey Manager 7 is one of the best simulation games that I have played. It's not quite as in-depth as it's cousin Out of the Park Baseball 21, but it's far and away better than most simulation games out there that I have played. 

Personally, I wish the playoff formats were more customizable like they are in OotP Baseball, and I think the manual for FHM7 doesn't go into as much detail as the one for OotP Baseball does. Sometimes when I can't figure out what a term is or a feature is supposed to do, I just have to guess or play with it until I figure it out for myself. There's been a few times where I searched for something in the manual only to come up empty. 

I've also had issues with player portraits. They never load properly and tend to only show up as a square of team color. I've also had a few crashes, but the auto save system is frequent enough on the default settings to where I've never lost anything significant. However, it does crash more than it should.

Despite this small issue, I've loved every minute in this game. The customization that is available is fun, and I find myself getting excited/nervous about whether or not my team will win a game and advance closer to the playoffs. I've never had that feeling with Madden or NBA2k. 

My only hope at this point is that Out of the Park Developments tackles the other 2 of the Big 4 Sports. Football and Basketball. If a Out of the Park Football game was created and it had as much depth as FHM7, I'd pay triple the price without question. Same thing with a Out of the Park Basketball. 

I'd highly recommend FHM7 to anyone who is interested in sports simulation, as well as Out of the Park Baseball 21. Both are incredible games and Out of the Park Developments is quickly becoming one of my favorite developers.

I owned FHM5 and FHM6 as well, and I must say this series is spectacular as a hockey fan. It goes so far in depth - 10x what you get from simming a GM Mode on Chel. And they keep adding significant changes every year, including this one!

The game has improved a lot from FHM6. UI, Simulations and small things such as scouting are streamlined without losing the depth it had. Overall it's still a really enjoyable game and worthy upgrade from 6 to 7 more so then 5 to 6. The issue I currently have is that I am getting maybe a crash every 30 minutes of gameplay which is just unacceptable. I would love to have more hours then I currently do but I just simply don't want to keep dealing with the crashes. Might play FHM6 till it is fixed.

I was able to find a forum post that for some reason told me to go into the settings and to go to Troubleshooting and click on Enable Debug Trace. For some reason my game is crash free now so if you are getting a lot of crashes I would suggest trying that first.

The game is definitely an improvement on older versions, but having to move the NHL Entry Draft into July, after the start of free agency in order to get expansion working nicely is not worthwhile in my opinion. The game is also very unstable. It crashes seemingly out of nowhere, with no indication as to why it's crashing. If you do get it, have it auto-save every week

- I have been playing a franchise now for a number of years, it randomly crashed and I can't load my recent save. Very frustrating for I've lost many hours of progress.

After 2 hours of play game, FHM7 didn't get me the same feeling than its predecessor. UI is way uglier than FHM6, facegen pictures are broken (there is some black holes in the generated picture), the game is very slow when simulating.

The new 2D sim engine has its issues, but that's to be expected with any brand new system. The new scouting system is great and allows you to easily see how well your scouts will scout certain areas. The game is overall fun and i'll probably play 100+ hours on it
Best hockey management game there is and they make improvements every year. If you enjoy sports managements games you will likely enjoy this one too. I'm excited for FHM 8 to release.

Each iteration brings new improvements, and this is no exception. Loving the 2D gameplay - only a matter of time before FHM is as refined as OOTP. Definitely worth supporting these guys, and the great work they do! High recommendation for me, for any fan of hockey, and or sports simulation.

BIG fan of this series. Ive played the out of the park baseball series for years and got FHM6 for the first time last year. Played it tones for months and months and it was a lot of fun. The new scouting system is a lot nicer and some other changes look great. Excited to get playing.

There were some good upgrades from 6 to 7. Things made easier. I still think the AI trading could be slightly better. Far too often you get an offer that is surprisingly lame. Especially for a high talented or high prospect. Well worth the upgrade.

It will always get compared to OOTP. While not quite as complex. The level of detail is amazing. I wish the 2D sim was a little more realistic. Overall a great game and if 2D sim isn't your thing, that minor upgrade won't matter to you anyway. 

There were a few bugs that were quickly addressed (During 2D sim showing the same player committing penalties when a different player was actually committing the infraction) being one

The new 2d game screen adds to the experience by showing all action during the game.  Over time, it might be smoothed out so the puck glides on the screen like on  ice, but it's still an improvement over the former game screen.  Stats are realistic and deep.

Very good so far. Will update the review after playing some more. Love the historical editing options, so I can change leagues and formats of past NHL seasons. Also great to see all the correct jerseys and logo's for the teams of the past. UI seems cleaner and better organized too. Haven't yet tried out 2D much yet. I hope the ice rink size will change according to era and American or European setting. The Player Icons seem a bit small on the ice, and adding names would also be great. Loving the experience so far.
I have played since FHM 4. There are enoigh changes in the system to make it worth it if you really enjoy this game and sports sim

It's a decent game. I'm writing this review from the perspective of someone who's relatively new to hockey. If you have been holding a stick and skating since you were 3 and are an absolute encyclopedia of pro hockey, both the game, history, and strategy, I would imagine you'd be quite pleased (version 10 is out as of this writing). My criticism of the game is that it's almost TOO realistic. There are easier modes and you can give a lot of responsibility to an assistant, but if you don't follow the NHL or other pro hockey very closely with an encyclopedic knowledge, you probably will be blown away by the complexity and options. I know the game of hockey itself rather well but the complexities of being a GM and coach, including roster building, managing scouting, contracts, majors/minors, free agency was overwhelming for me and put me off from playing it for a while, so just be prepared for that. I never bought v8 or v9 but am considering 10. The other disappointment (which I hear has been changed in recent versions) is that while you can create custom leagues, it's not very user-friendly. When selecting the league format, there's nothing telling you how the playoff format will work, is it division, is it wild card. And also I was hoping to just create a fictional league with dropping in real teams. Can't do that. Have my own league but still use AHL/CHL as farm leagues...can't do that. Play through an Olympic tournament as a one-off without a league. Can't do that. So creation is good but needs some work for flexibility.

Bottom line: Probably very great for hockey enthusiast. But if you're not an encyclopedia on pro hockey you can get lost in the complexity very quickly. Too many things are not explained, the menu system is not user-friendly, and the customization (the main selling point for me) is good but too inflexible and not well-documented. I'd give it 4.5 potential but 2.5 ability, because I think this CAN be the best hockey game franchise out there if it were better documented, simpler to operate, had difficulty levels and better customization

I've been playing this game since EHM.  Each time I get the itch to play it I sink some more hours in, play through a couple of seasons, and then feel hollow afterwards.  There isn't enough feedback on tactics, owner expectations, or career progression.  Trading mechanics are decent, but the AI consistently makes bad decisions when trading with other AI teams.  Trading is also slanted in the AI's favor as the over-value assets and require too much in return.  Scouting is improved over previous versions.  Tactics are my biggest complaint as they seem to make little difference in outcomes and there's no real way to know if they're working or not.  There isn't really a point to playing the games out as there isn't any control in-game to adjust tactics or make changes.  It seems like a lot of these issues have been addressed in FHM 9, so I'm sure I'll crack and try that one next.
Its a great game it just crashed mid way through a playthrough on my M1 Mac and won't let me play anymore. I'm really frustrated.

Better each edition. While the 3D gameview is very basic, it is still much better for being able to adjust strategy because you can see how the computer is playing rather than guessing off of text descriptions of the action. The manager interface and roster/training options are good. The sense of seeing your team progress as you build the roster and "coach 'em up" is very satisfying if you're a die-hard hockey fan that dreams of guiding a team to glory. Worth every penny many times over.

Played a little bit of present day, got bored. Then I got through 2 seasons of historical, but now it crashes every time I try to pass 6/30. The in-game version is total crap, it doesn't look like the flow of hockey even a little bit so the only way to play is pure sim which is somewhat tolerable. Penalties in general aren't believable... people get misconducts after silly things like a hooking penalty, but never see them in games where it became a bit of a brawl. Speaking of which, there never are any even if you play in the 70's and 80's when they had them all the time.  Trading pretty much never happens. No way to set what you want back, so you constantly get offers back for some 35 year old half-star player instead of a draft pick that would help you.  Speaking of trades, most trade deadlines go by with maybe 1 trade if any.

But I could overlook most of that if the game was really good.  But it's not... not by a long shot. The UI is one of the clunkiest I've ever seen... No easy ways to bounce between your farm teams, most right-click menus have like 23 options on them. No click and drag at all. No re-size ability on the game window. News gets overwhelming with the shear number of "who gives a crap" updates, so I end up ignoring most of it (which causes me to miss something I DO want to see.

It's too bad. I had hopes for this game as OOTP has a really good baseball sim.

Very enjoyable and well detailed game that allows you to take over just about any hockey team you can think of and try and lead them to a Championship. The game does have a "secret formula" or way to become champions fast but to discover this took me many seasons and i still find myself learning new things after 1000+ hours. 

The Development team for this game is dedicated and are just a message or post any from being able to help you and I have never had any issue they couldn't solve instantly and that's not as common as some people think so very happy to play this game all the time and recommend it :)

I think this is a fantastic game, for what it is. 

That's really the most important thing potential purchasers need to know. This is NOT EA Sports NHL series. You do NOT control the actual hockey gameplay. You do everything but that.

So if you want to control your players on the ice, this game isn't for you. If you are a person who likes Be A GM mode in the EA NHL series, this game is very much for you. This is Be A GM Mode on steroids.

Do you want to take on the Seattle Kraken in their inaugural season and guide them to a championship by 2025? You can do that.

Do you want to assume control of the Hartford Whalers when the WHA folded up in 1979? Doing that right now. It's great. I managed to win the Cup by '82 through good drafting and development (Hello, Paul Coffey, Andy Moog, and Bernie Nicholls!) and a few blockbuster trades (Mark Howe for Mike Gartner, straight up).

You can shepherd teams in leagues across the world. Pick a KHL team, or a Deutsche League team. Pick any country in the world and run their national team.

And I'll tell ya, the player stats and development is GOOD. Like "consistently surprising me" with how good it is. As an Avalanche fan, for example, I wouldn't expect virtually anyone else to know 3rd round prospect from 2019, Alex Beaucage. Beaucage is a guy with a wicked shot but is a bad skater. That is totally represented in this game.

As a hockey nerd, if you are one, you will consistently appreciate that attention to detail.

Graphically, this game is nothing to write home about. It's a game you mostly play in a series of menus and stat sheets. As long as you know that, and like it, you will like this game.

A fantastic sport management game, a must for any hockey fans!

Maybe it doesn't have a gameplay element like EA's NHL series but this is so much more fulfilling from a managerial standpoint. There's legitimate trade logic, there's the ability to screw around with conferences and alignment, there's a freaking GOD MODE, and all of the roster and contract rules, limits and implications are present; no movement/trade clauses exist, the cap is way more in-depth, there's an actual IR and injuries aren't flukey. In NHL they seem to happen once a game, at least, here, they aren't as rampant.

The managerial aspect is what a franchise mode is all about, and this game captures all of it better than any of the EA sports titles have. An astute user will notice that year by year, the logos are updated exactly when the normally are, and you can even implement CUSTOM LOGOS, something not even the console games allow for. You really have the freedom to play god in this game, and I truly love what they've done. It feels way more true to what being an actual NHL coach, GM or owner would be, it remains faithful to that while still allowing you the free reign a video game should. This is cool, well worth it, especially if the console "simulations" go for $60 at release, this is an awesome deal, and it doesn't even need a god mode rig to run well. Good job boys!

The Procedural Generation of maps and the grid-based placement system leaves a lot of room for player optimization. These are not game-breaking issues and therefore I hate to give a negative rating to this nice looking and principally coherent game.

However, the game lacks one crucial feature: the joy of playing!

Everybody who has ever played a Tower Defense game will beat this one on the first try. You play 35 waves on a randomly generated map and then...
Well, then the game is over.
The options that remain are either to continue playing in endless mode (basically letting the game run to get a coffee) or start a new game on another randomly generated map. Basically not a bad game principle, only the player is not rewarded.

What the game urgently needs is a kind of progress model. E.g. levels or stages by which the enemies get stronger, or the maps get bigger, or you unlock new turrets, or you have to survive more waves, or, or, or...

The game has potential and the basic game mechanics work well, but in the current state of the game, there is simply no reason for the player to click on Start again after the first run.
